text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Senior politburo member Le Kha Phieu says economic support to families of war martyrs and invalids will be increased in line with Vietnam's economic growth rates.
-- Vietnam reported a trade deficit of $1.77 billion and industrial growth of 13.8 percent in the first seven months of this year.
-- Vietnam's biggest commercial bank, Vietcombank say it is still enjoying good fiscal health despite a slight slowdown in the first six months of 1997.
-- South Korea's LG group plans to invest a further $300 million towards expanding its activities in Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines.

-- The Construction Ministry has approved detailed infrastructure development plans for the Dung Quat Industrial Park, including a $18.8 million road linking the proposed Dung Quat oil refinery with National Highway 1.
-- The National Election Council says 99.59 percent of eligible voters took part in last week's National Assembly election.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has called for countries involved in disputes over territory in the South China Sea to maintain the status quo by exercising restraint.
-- A Nepal Communist Party delegation has begun an official visit to Hanoi to strengthen relations of friendship and cooperation between the two parties and two countries.
-- Ho Chi Minh City has invested $19.58 million to upgrade the city's power network since the end of 1996.
